claims.text: The initial material is an additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 high-entropy alloy with dual nanoprecipitation.
The nanoprecipitates are uniformly distributed in the alloy matrix.
High-temperature oxidation induces nanoscale elemental redistribution within and around the nanoprecipitates.
Elemental redistribution around the nanoprecipitates contributes to formation of protective oxide phases.
Oxidation treatments at relevant high temperatures promote elemental diffusion and oxide-scale formation.
High-temperature oxidation causes selective elemental migration in the alloy.
Al, Cr, and Ti are oxidation-resistant species in the stated alloy context.
Al, Cr, or Ti become enriched at nanoprecipitate–matrix interfaces during oxidation.
Interfacial enrichment of oxidation-resistant elements facilitates development of a protective oxide scale.
Oxidation may alter the internal composition of the nanoprecipitates.
Atom probe tomography can produce three-dimensional elemental maps across and near nanoprecipitates.
APT will detect compositional gradients at and around nanoprecipitates after oxidation.
The detected redistribution will correlate with enhanced oxidation resistance.
Oxidized samples will show localized enrichment of oxidation-resistant elements relative to unoxidized samples.
Changes in temperature, oxygen partial pressure, or exposure time may change redistribution dynamics or produce additional phases.
APT specimen preparation may affect the observed elemental gradients.
